svg.text: Band-edge spacing boundary after the first adjacent-loop test

At fixed loop gain and fixed 0 dB adjacent power, spacing alone reveals two different boundaries: when the half-sine lane becomes track-ready again, and when it finally stops being the worse loop on mean residual.
The spacing sweep split one fuzzy “boundary” into two clean ones

text.tspan: Same bounded loop as the last adjacent-channel note: SRRC QPSK, 4 samples/symbol, 63-tap band-edge filters, one blockwise loop with gain 0.02, and adjacent power fixed at 0 dB. The only knob moving now is channel
spacing.

svg.text: 1.00 R_s: half-sine is still the worse loop

text.tspan: Proxy averages 0.0387 R_s with 100% of the tail inside ±0.05 R_s. Half-sine
averages 0.0995 R_s with only 0%.

svg.text: 1.24 R_s: half-sine gets back inside the settle band

text.tspan: At about 1.24 R_s, every tail block is back inside ±0.05 R_s for the
half-sine lane, even though its mean pull is still higher than the proxy
lane.

svg.text: 1.57 R_s: the residual ranking finally flips

text.tspan: Only around 1.57 R_s does the half-sine mean tail pull (0.0002 R_s) edge
below the proxy value (0.0002 R_s).

svg.text: Mean tail residual CFO versus spacing

text.tspan: Lower is better. The half-sine lane improves rapidly as the neighbor moves away, but it does not actually
beat the proxy on this metric until the spacing is much larger than the first “track-ready again” point.

svg.text: How much of the tail stays inside ±0.05 R_s?

text.tspan: This is the same bounded settle-quality summary as before: count the last eight loop blocks and ask what
fraction stay inside the ±0.05 R_s band. Here the first sharp boundary arrives earlier than the
mean-residual crossover.

The earlier note proved that the half-sine lane lost under the fixed 1.0 R_s stress case. This spacing sweep answers the next sharper question: the ranking does not flip at one magical point unless the metric is named
first. Track-ready settle behavior comes back around 1.24 R_s, while the stricter mean-residual ranking does not flip until about 1.57 R_s.
• Proxy: 0.0387 R_s, 100% inside band.
• Half-sine: 0.0995 R_s, 0% inside band.
• Half-sine tail fraction reaches 100% with mean pull 0.0447 R_s.
• Proxy is already calm there at 0.0028 R_s.
• Half-sine mean pull 0.0002 R_s finally edges below proxy 0.0002 R_s.
• That is the honest “preference flip” point for this stricter metric.
